title: Artificial Intelligence and Public Standards: government response to report
description: The government's response to the Committee's 2020 report Artificial Intelligence and Public Standards
summary: The government has issued a response to the 2020 Committee report on artificial intelligence and public standards, outlining its approach to improving AI governance. It highlights key areas such as accountability, transparency, and collaboration with industry to ensure AI technologies benefit society.

title: ​​Ofqual’s approach to regulating the use of artificial intelligence in the qualifications sector​
description: Published in response to a request from the Secretary of State for Education, the Secretary of State for Science, Innovation and Technology, and the Secretary of State for Business and Trade.
summary: Ofqual has outlined how it will oversee and set rules for using artificial intelligence in the qualifications sector, aiming to maintain fairness and integrity in exams and assessments. The policy was released after a joint request from the Secretary of State for Education, Science, Innovation and Technology, and Business and Trade.

title: Report and impact assessment on Copyright and Artificial Intelligence
description: A report and impact assessment on the use of copyright works in the development of artificial intelligence (AI) systems.
summary: This report examines how copyright-protected works are used to train and develop AI systems, exploring the legal, economic, and social implications of such practices. It offers recommendations for balancing creators' rights with the benefits of AI innovation.

title: Government response to the House of Lords Select Committee on Artificial Intelligence
description: Government response to the Lords Select Committee on Artificial Intelligence report ‘AI in the UK: No Room for Complacency’.
summary: The UK government responded to the House of Lords Select Committee’s report “AI in the UK: No Room for Complacency” by outlining its plans to strengthen AI regulation, safety, and ethical standards while supporting innovation. It pledges to invest in research, improve public trust, and collaborate with industry to build a responsible AI ecosystem that benefits all citizens.

title: AI and Public Standards – Terms of Reference
description: Terms of Reference and FAQs for the Committee's review into artificial intelligence and public standards.
summary: This document outlines the purpose and scope of a committee tasked with reviewing how artificial intelligence intersects with public standards, and provides FAQs to guide stakeholders. It sets out the committee’s responsibilities, the review process, and key questions to address.

title: CSPL submission to Science and Technology Committee inquiry on Governance of AI
description: CSPL has submitted written evidence to the Science and Technology Committee's inquiry on Governance of Artificial Intelligence.
summary: CSPL has submitted written evidence to the Science and Technology Committee’s inquiry on the governance of artificial intelligence. The submission aims to inform and influence policy discussions around AI regulation and oversight.

title: Impact of AI on the regulation of medical products
description: Implementing the Artificial Intelligence (AI) White Paper principles.
summary: This policy explains how artificial intelligence will influence and improve the regulation of medical products, aiming to keep them safe, effective, and trustworthy while encouraging innovation. It urges the adoption of the AI White Paper principles to shape regulatory frameworks, risk assessment, and transparency for AI‑driven healthcare technologies.

title: Defence Artificial Intelligence Strategy
description: Our vision is that, in terms of AI, we will be the world’s most effective, efficient, trusted and influential Defence organisation for our size.
summary: The Defence Artificial Intelligence Strategy sets out how the organisation will use AI to become the most effective, efficient, trusted, and influential defence player in the world for its size. It focuses on developing and deploying AI capabilities that enhance national security, operational readiness, and innovation across the defence sector.

title: Transport artificial intelligence action plan
description: Sets out how DfT will work with the transport sector to exploit the opportunities from AI while managing potential risks.
summary: The Transport Artificial Intelligence Action Plan explains how the UK Department for Transport will partner with the transport sector to harness the benefits of AI technology. It also details measures to identify, mitigate, and manage the risks that AI could pose to safety, privacy, and security within transport systems.

title: Copyright and artificial intelligence: progress report
description: A progress report on the use of copyright works in the development of AI systems, under Section 137 of the Data (Use and Access) Act.
summary: This report reviews how copyright‑protected works are used to train AI models, assessing compliance with the Data (Use and Access) Act’s Section 137. It highlights progress made, challenges faced, and recommends steps for balancing copyright protection with AI innovation.
